bullets: Game 1 of a six-game single-deck session, and Ryley names it in the opening line: 'we are going to be playing the best Hog Rider Earthquake deck in Clash Royale' (t=6-9). The eighth slot is Earthquake, not the Heal Spirit the pipeline's HUD consensus reported — he casts three Earthquakes into the opponent's half (clock 0:08, OT 0:57, OT 0:29) and Heal Spirit is never named or tiled. Closest KB list: barbarian-barrel-cannon-earthquake-electro-spirit-firecracker-hog-rider-mighty-miner-skeletons, sharing seven of eight cards.

Piloted as a one-lane cycle deck: the opening Hog goes left at clock 2:46 for 507 damage, and after that every Hog and every spell goes right, into the tower the opponent has already committed against. His own left tower finishes the game at full 4858 HP — the opponent never attacked it.

Defence is a fixed pattern rather than card-by-card improvisation: Evo Cannon in the middle columns of his own half (eight placements, [8, 9] to [9, 10], plus a deep [12, 2] against the big golem), Skeletons or Electro Spirit as the body, The Log for the ground clutter, Mighty Miner + ability for the tank. He replays the Cannon on cooldown — 'Cannon number three of the defense' (t=145).

The deck's weakness shows at clock 1:49: an Elixir Golem + Night Witch + Freeze push takes his right tower from 4858 to 2536 in twenty seconds, and he ends regular time behind on damage (own right 2065 vs enemy right 2916) at 0-0 crowns.

It wins in overtime on chip discipline: he holds the Hog twice against the Evo Skeleton Army ('I really want to go Hog Rider here, but I know it's not worth it', t=196-199), pairs each Hog with an Earthquake as a Skarmy prediction, and uses the Evo Firecracker to bait Vines. Enemy right tower 2916 -> 129 while his own sits at 591; 'let's go for the earthquake. Let's go. Very nice win' (t=271-272).

new_deck.rationale: Seven of the eight cards cost 1-3 elixir and the deck wins by replaying a 4-elixir Hog Rider plus a 3-elixir Earthquake every rotation rather than by building one push.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The cheap four-card cycle of Skeletons, Electro Spirit, The Log and Earthquake means the Hog Rider is back in hand before the opponent's building or swarm is, which is exactly how this game is won: eight Evo Cannon placements and eleven Skeletons deploys absorb an Elixir Golem beatdown deck while the Hog collects a couple of hits every rotation. Evo Cannon in the middle columns covers both lanes for 3 elixir, so a beatdown opponent cannot force a lane commitment, and Mighty Miner's Explosive Escape gives the deck a tank-killer and a swarm answer in one card. Earthquake does the deck's real thinking: behind a bridge Hog it is both chip and a pre-emptive Skeleton Army answer, which is what closes this match (t=237 and t=264). The known hole is a big supported tank plus Freeze — one such push here cost 2300 tower HP and forced overtime.
